name: @fps-games/editor-agent-mcp

tools.name: list_editor_sessions
tools.description: List editor pages currently connected to the local Agent Bridge WebSocket. Start here after get_bridge_health; if no session exists, use browser fallback only to open or refresh the editor page, then return to MCP tools.

tools.name: list_editor_capabilities
tools.description: List Agent Bridge capabilities exposed by an active editor session. Read each manifest description, access, inputSchema, and outputSchema before calling a capability.

tools.name: call_editor_capability
tools.description: Call one Agent Bridge capability on an active editor session. Use host.editor.enter as the default L1 entry point; use asset.library.list/asset.analysis.get before object.createFromAsset; use prefab.scene.get and prefab.node.* inside Prefab Stage; browser automation is fallback only.

tools.name: get_bridge_health
tools.description: Read local Agent Bridge MCP, WebSocket, admin console, session, and registered tool health. Use this first to decide whether the MCP/bridge layer is available before falling back to browser automation.

tools.name: run_editor_bridge_smoke_test
tools.description: Run a readonly MCP-to-editor Agent Bridge smoke test against an active editor session. It validates required L1/L2 manifests, reports L2 core, camera, asset, prefab composition, and Shadow V2 manifest coverage, and calls only editor.state.get for the roundtrip.

instructions:
FPS Editor Agent Bridge exposes a stable MCP protocol surface over dynamic editor capabilities.
MCP tools are the stable agent-facing layer; editor actions live in runtime-discovered Editor Bridge capabilities.
Standard workflow: call get_bridge_health, then list_editor_sessions, then list_editor_capabilities, then call_editor_capability.
For editor workspace orientation, call editor.ui.regions.get after capability discovery. It maps top Toolbar, left Hierarchy, center Preview/Scene View, right Inspector/render tabs, bottom Asset Library, and Agent Bridge Console to preferred capabilities.
To enter or ensure editor mode, prefer call_editor_capability with capabilityId host.editor.enter. Use host.editor.waitReady only when extra readiness confirmation or timeout diagnostics are needed.
After host.editor.enter reports editorReady=true, use L2 Core Editing capabilities such as scene.objects.list, object.resolve, editor.snapshot.get, transform.move, transform.set, viewport.focusObject, viewport.frameSelection, object.createPrimitive, and object.delete.
Region semantics: left Hierarchy maps to scene.objects.list/object.resolve/selection.set; in Prefab Stage it maps to prefab.scene.get/prefab.node.select/prefab.node.rename/prefab.node.createGroup/prefab.node.createPrimitive/prefab.node.reparent/prefab.node.delete; center Preview is a scoped visual editing surface: scene scope maps to viewport.camera.*, viewport.focusObject, viewport.frameSelection, transform.move, and transform.set, while Prefab Stage scope maps preview selection/transform to prefab.node.select and prefab.node.setTransform; right Inspector maps to editor.state.get/editor.snapshot.get/transform.set and future property capabilities; bottom Asset Library maps to asset.library.list/asset.info.get/asset.analysis.get/prefab.resolve/prefab.stage.open/prefab.stage.exit/object.createFromAsset/prefab.node.createFromAsset; top Toolbar maps to host.* and editor state capabilities.
For assets, use L2 Asset Placement & Analysis capabilities: asset.library.list to find standard assets, asset.info.get for serializable catalog metadata, asset.analysis.get for SDK-generated GLB/image structure summaries, then object.createFromAsset to create placeable assets through the editor harness path.
For Prefab Composition, discover prefab assets with asset.library.list kind=prefab or prefab.resolve, open the Prefab stage with prefab.stage.open, inspect editable composition with prefab.scene.get, rename the prefab asset/displayName with prefab.asset.rename, rename non-root editable nodes with prefab.node.rename, add empty group nodes with prefab.node.createGroup, add child model or prefab assets with prefab.node.createFromAsset, add primitive helpers with prefab.node.createPrimitive, edit local transforms with prefab.node.setTransform, move hierarchy with prefab.node.reparent, remove nodes with prefab.node.delete, inspect readonly GLB/source anatomy with prefab.source.structure.get, inspect material targets with prefab.materialSlots.list, then return with prefab.stage.exit. These are Editor Bridge capabilities, not MCP tools.
In Prefab Stage Preview, editable projection nodes map back to prefab composition nodes. Use prefab.node.select and prefab.node.setTransform for semantic editing; Source Structure, readonly nodes, and comparison preview projections are visual/read-only evidence, not transform targets.
Rename domains are explicit: prefab.asset.rename changes the prefab asset displayName and Prefab Stage root label; prefab.node.rename changes editable composition nodes only; scene object names use the scene object rename path when available; GLB Source Structure names are readonly anatomy and must not be renamed.
For Shadow System V2, use shadow.policy.get, shadow.receivers.list, and shadow.resolvePreview before edits; use shadow.policy.set for scene objects, prefab roots/nodes, or prefab instances. Prefer shared prefab defaults under prefab.defaults.shadow.* and keep per-instance shadow overrides for local exceptions. User-facing object Inspector only exposes concise shadow presets: high performance, balanced, and high quality; project-level shadow params/backends live in the Rendering / Shadows tab. Legacy shadowMode is compatibility-only and should not be used as a new authoring surface. Static baked shadow authoring entry points are currently hidden while that workflow is redesigned; use dynamic/blob/projected/debug capabilities for current validation.
Directional Light orientation is framework-synchronized: transform.rotation.x is elevation radians, transform.rotation.y is horizontal radians, and light.direction is the canonical runtime/shadow direction. Use transform.set to author Directional Light rotation, then verify with shadow.resolvePreview or shadow.debug.inspect. If light.orientationDiagnostics reports shadow.lightOrientationDrift, treat it as legacy data drift and edit the light orientation through transform/inspector paths instead of trusting screenshots.
For shadow debugging, do not judge from a screenshot alone. Prefer shadow.debug.context.enter: it preserves the caster, resolved receivers, shadow light, and ambient/environment lights, hides unrelated projections, protects receivers from accidental hiding, applies receiver/footprint/light overlays, and returns shadow.debug.inspect plus shadow.debug.visibilityMeasure evidence. Use viewport.isolation.enter or viewport.visibility.* only as lower-level fallback. Clear the debug view with shadow.debug.context.clear before continuing normal editing.
For projected/planar shadow contour debugging, inspect shadow.debug.inspect.runtimeEvidence.planar before relying on pixels. The internal auto strategy should prefer projected mesh with alpha cutout for ordinary and skinned meshes, and only fall back to convex hull with fallbackReasons when cloning/geometry/budget constraints require it. Record strategy, projectedMeshCount, convexHullMeshCount, alphaCutoutMeshCount, alphaCutoutChannels, alphaCutoutUvSets, alphaCutoutLevels, and fallbackReasons; do not add a new user-facing shadow mode to bypass planar algorithm defects.
For stable visual inspection, prefer L2 View/Camera capabilities viewport.camera.get, viewport.camera.setPreset, and viewport.camera.orbit before using browser screenshots.
For multi-step work, pass the same optional traceId and a human-readable traceLabel to MCP tools. The daemon records MCP calls, capability calls, diagnostics, and safe summaries in the Agent Operation Trace.
When L0 browser or desktop fallback is required, write screenshot paths, console/page errors, and brief before/after evidence to POST /api/traces/events on the local admin console; do not embed screenshot bytes or raw asset contents.
L3 workflow capabilities are deferred until repeated real L1/L2 call chains justify a stable workflow API.
Use Playwright, Chrome DevTools, or other browser automation only as L0 fallback: no bridge health, no editor session, missing host.editor.enter or target capability, capability unavailable/timeout, or visual screenshot verification.
If browser fallback opens or refreshes a page, return to the MCP/capability workflow as soon as a session is registered.
Use run_editor_bridge_smoke_test before debugging Codex tool snapshots or editor bridge connectivity.
Do not assume every editor operation is an MCP tool; most editor actions are capabilities discovered at runtime.
